title: Parents, Teachers, and Coaches: Where Do Mindsets Come From?
coreMove: Adults transmit mindset through what they praise, what they criticize, how high they aim, and whether they give learners better strategies after failure.

exampleSpecs.domain: parent response after a homework win
exampleSpecs.stakes: a child may protect the smart label instead of choosing challenge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use the seven praise experiments with children to shift from intelligence praise to process praise

exampleSpecs.audience: teachers choosing between comfort and demand
exampleSpecs.stakes: students labeled low may receive thin work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Marva Collins to pair demanding material with belief and instruction

exampleSpecs.domain: youth orchestra rehearsal after repeated mistakes
exampleSpecs.audience: teachers and coaches giving corrective feedback
exampleSpecs.stakes: students could feel either guided or shamed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Rafe Esquith and Dorothy DeLay as models of rigorous patient development

exampleSpecs.domain: club basketball practice after sloppy defense
exampleSpecs.stakes: players may learn fear rather than responsibility
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Bobby Knight and John Wooden to separate winning pressure from growth climate

exampleSpecs.stakes: students may hear effort praise without better instruction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use false growth mindset correction to reject empty effort praise

exampleSpecs.stakes: soft feedback could leave the student without a repair path
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use process praise and honest criticism to name what failed and what to try next
